title: Agents That Own Their Inference — Du'an Lightfoot & Khaja Omer, Akamai Technologies
talk_summary: A workshop on self-hosting LLM inference on dedicated GPUs with vLLM: sizing model weights vs KV cache, quantization, speculative decoding, and tuning concurrency flags.

takeaways.technique: Per-change eval gate before swapping model/precision
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist on running your own eval set (JSON validity, function-call success, loops/hallucination checks) before and after any model or quantization change, rather than trusting benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very important that you have your own eval set and you're running your own evals to make sure any changes you make

takeaways.technique: Prompt caching for recurring agent loops
takeaways.what_they_do: For continuously running applications, cache the stable prompt prefix at the provider to cut token cost; distinguish provider prompt caching from local prefix caching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prompt caching is a must, right? You can you can decrease the cost by like up to 75%

takeaways.what_they_do: Thinking mode ballooned a 35-token answer to ~600 tokens; they recommend setting an explicit thinking-token budget where the model supports it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with thinking on now, it had to think about it. It cost about 600 tokens

takeaways.technique: Observability spans per tool call to diagnose small-model inefficiency
takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument every agent step/tool call with token counts and latency (self-hosted Langfuse) so they can see when a smaller model makes too many tool calls and then specialize the prompt or trim tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can see, okay, I'm using a smaller model and it's making way more tool calls

takeaways.technique: Measure the concurrency 'knee' before scaling hardware
takeaways.what_they_do: Load-test at increasing concurrency and find the point where throughput flattens but latency spikes; tune max-num-seqs to push that knee out rather than adding GPUs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you essentially want to find the sweet spot
takeaways.numbers: at 64 concurrency: 800→1100 tok/s and 2000ms→800ms latency after raising max-num-seqs

takeaways.technique: Speculative decoding only with matched drafter
takeaways.what_they_do: They show speculative decoding can tank performance (58→16 tok/s) when the draft model isn't trained for the target model, and that acceptance rate must be measured per use case.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this particular drapher model is not trained correctly for this particular model
